status_summary: VA lists the Office of Human Resources and Administration and the Office of Operations, Security, and Preparedness as separate staff offices with separate leaders (page last updated 2026-02-25), and its biography of Reginald G. A. Neal says the President appointed him Assistant Secretary for Operations, Security, and Preparedness in December 2025, while Mark Engelbaum serves as Assistant Secretary for Human Resources and Administration. In a written statement to a House Veterans' Affairs subcommittee on 2026-06-24, VA said it is completing a reorganization that gives the security office its own Assistant Secretary and a unified chain of command for VA Police. No order, Federal Register notice or effective date of the separation was found, so the record treats the separation as operative in substance through the separate offices and appointments, with the wider reorganization still described as in progress.

timeline.event: The President appointed an Assistant Secretary for Operations, Security, and Preparedness, a post held separately from the Assistant Secretary for Human Resources and Administration (month-only date: December 2025, per the VA biography).

title: Consider separating VA's HR and Administration office from Security and Preparedness
uncertainties: The VA rule list on reginfo.gov (labeled Agency Rule List - 2026, 62 rules) lists no rulemaking on staff office structure, which would be internal. The separation rests on VA pages and a 2026-06-24 VA statement to Congress; no order, Federal Register notice or effective date was found, and the statement describes the reorganization as being completed. VA's stated purpose is a unified VA Police chain of command, not the staffing rationale the Mandate gives; the record reports alignment only. Some VA URLs still carry the combined office name. Whether the second Assistant Secretary position needed statutory change was not checked. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19. Refutation check on 2026-10-25: a news report dated 2026-06-25 (Air Force Times) says the police consolidation under the Office of Operations, Security, and Preparedness was announced that week and that officials expected the reorganization to be completed by October; it names no memo or order, so the effective date of the separation remains unknown and the reorganization may still have been in progress at the 2026-10-25 check. The department.va.gov offices page, fetched again, lists the Office of Human Resources and Administration and the Office of Operations, Security, and Preparedness as separate entries with separate named leaders. Federal Register API queries for VA documents naming either office (since 2025-06 and all years) returned no organizational notice or order; a 2026-01-15 Privacy Act notice mentions the security office only in passing. Review 2026-10-25: the 2026-06-24 VA written statement was moved out of the timeline because testimony describing a reorganization is not itself a government action; it stays in sources and supports the separate Assistant Secretary posts. The appointment event uses a month-only date from the VA biography (updated 2025-12-08), which does not say whether the appointment was Senate-confirmed or acting.
